key_insight: The paper shows that distributed quantum computing can be made scalable by using a weak-coupling approximation, reducing classical reconstruction cost from exponential to polynomial.
engineering_relevance: This enables more practical partitioned execution of quantum circuits on distributed hardware, especially for QAOA-like layered workloads.
method: Partition the quantum procedure around a qubit that is weakly coupled to the rest of the circuit.
Use a controlled approximation to reconstruct the distributed quantum process with polynomial classical overhead.
Demonstrate the approach on layered circuits inspired by quantum approximate optimization algorithm circuits.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a demonstration on layered QAOA-style circuits and claims the classical cost drops from exponential to polynomial under the weak-coupling partitioning assumption.
watch_item: The approach depends on a weak-coupling structure, so accuracy and scalability may degrade if the circuit does not satisfy that assumption well.
paper_title: Scalable quantum circuit knitting using a weak-coupling approximation
